verdict: CONFIRMED — middleware.ts (~378-385) forwards bearer requests unvalidated, app/api/market/prices/[symbol]/route.ts and app/api/market/spx/route.ts check only verifySecuritiesImportToken with no rateLimit call (grep across app/api confirms only strategy/tune uses the limiter), and src/lib/history.ts fetchDailyOHLC (lines 85-126) cascades up to 6 network providers per miss with a 30-min positive cache but no negative caching, so unknown-symbol requests re-run the full cascade every time; only the Massive tier is self-throttled (reserveMassiveRestCall, line 172).
correctedDetail: The two token-gated peer read routes (/api/market/prices/{symbol}, /api/market/spx) have no rate limiting at any layer: middleware passes bearer requests through unvalidated and the handlers only verify APP_B_INGEST_TOKEN before invoking the full daily-OHLC cascade (App A → Massive → Tradier → Marketstack → Yahoo → Stooq — up to 6 upstream fetches). Refinement: the 30-minute in-process cache dampens repeat requests for symbols that resolve, but there is NO negative caching — every request for an unknown/unresolvable symbol re-runs the entire cascade, so a CT retry storm or catch-up loop iterating tickers (or a leaked token) drives unbounded fan-out into Tradier/Marketstack/Yahoo/Stooq and ST CPU; reserveMassiveRestCall protects only the Massive tier. Unauthenticated floods are cheap (constant-time compare + one audit row), so exploitation requires the shared secret or a misbehaving CT — medium severity stands. The proposed fix is sound: src/lib/rate-limit.ts already provides the in-process sliding-window limiter with retryAfterSeconds, matching the deployment's single-process model.
